answer: An agent economy can require tokens locked for 30 days to vote on shared spending, with voting power proportional to stake. Whether an agent inspects a bridge, maps a ledge, or writes a sonnet, creating more identities adds no votes: splitting 100 tokens among 100 agents still yields only 100 tokens of influence. To gain more power, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lock.
